title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (as reconstructed from this page and the neighbouring ones). Pi^ = pi^_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of U_{0,3} = P^1_Q minus {0,1,inf}. M_{0,3}^{!~} is the group of automorphisms of Pi^ that respect the inertia ('loop') classes up to a common power and commute outer-wise with the S_3 action (S_3 generated by sigma_inf and rho, with rho of order 3). It is an extension of N_{0,3}^{!~} by Pi^. Gamma_Q maps into it, and the Galois image is meant to sit inside this GT-like group. Rational or algebraic points q of U_{0,3} would give partial splittings of M over N above the stabilizer Gamma_Q(q). The previous page treated the S_3-special points q=1/2 (orbit 1/2, 2, -1) and q=-j (orbit -j, -j^2), whose splittings he had computed in cases 1 and 2.

What this page does.
- It turns to the cusps. M^{!~}[0] corresponds to the point 0 of the completed curve U^_{0,3} = P^1_Q. The analogous subgroups M^{!~}[1] and M^{!~}[inf] correspond to the other two points at infinity and are obtained by transporting M[0] by rho and rho^2.
- From the next page, M[q] is the normalizer in M^{!~} of the loop group L_q, the inertia subgroup of Pi^ at the cusp q, isomorphic to Z^(1).
- These subgroups are not strict partial sections of M over N. Their intersection with Pi^ is not trivial but equals L_0, L_1 or L_inf. This holds because inertia subgroups of a free profinite group are self-normalizing.
- So M[0] is an extension of N[0] by L_0, the analogue of the decomposition group D_0, which is Z^(1) semidirect Gamma_Q.
- Grothendieck recalls that choosing a uniformizer of the local ring of P^1 at 0 determines a splitting of M^{an}(0) as an extension of N by L_0. In arithmetic terms this is the section of the decomposition group given by Puiseux series in z^{1/n}, i.e. a tangential base point.
- He sets the programme: understand such a splitting, attached to a uniformizer, inside his explicit calculus. There an element is described by data (alpha, beta), or (eta, xi) on the next page, satisfying the 'relations des lacets'. The splitting should give a privileged way to normalize (alpha, beta) modulo L_0.

What this feeds into. The next page sets u(sigma_inf) = eta sigma_inf and u(rho) = xi rho, with u(eps_0) = eps_0^mu and mu - 1 = 2nu. This yields eta sigma(eta) = 1, xi rho(xi) rho^2(xi) = 1 and xi = eta l_1^nu, i.e. the 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations of the (profinite) Grothendieck–Teichmüller group. In modern terms, the remark on this page is that the indeterminacy of the GT pair (lambda, f) modulo inertia at 0 is removed by the tangential base point. This is Drinfeld's normalization of f in the commutator subgroup, and Ihara's choice of the tangential base point 01-> for the Galois representation into GT^.
errors: No real mathematical error. Gap: a uniformizer gives a canonical splitting only over the arithmetic (Galois) part, i.e. the decomposition group Z^(1) semidirect Gamma_Q. For the full abstract group N^{!~}[0] no such splitting is given, which is exactly what he says must still be 'grasped'.

Unstated nuance: the splitting depends on the uniformizer only through its tangent vector at 0. Rescaling z by c in Q* changes the section by the Kummer cocycle of c. The S_3-stabilizer of 0 (z -> z/(z-1)) sends the tangent vector to its negative, so compatibility with S_3 involves the Kummer character of -1.

ideas.what: Subgroups M[q] for the cusps q=0,1,inf, defined as normalizers of the inertia/loop groups L_q and permuted by rho; they are extensions of the base by L_q rather than sections
ideas.modern_name: decomposition groups at cusps (D_q, an extension by Z^(1)) inside the GT-type group
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard anabelian geometry; Ihara, Nakamura in the GT context
ideas.where_published: Longue Marche (1981) is the likely context; not checked

ideas.what: A uniformizer at a cusp determines a splitting of the decomposition-group extension
ideas.modern_name: tangential base point (Puiseux-series section of D_0)
ideas.where_published: possibly Esquisse d'un programme / Longue Marche; unsure

ideas.what: Using this splitting to give a privileged normalization of the loop-equation data (alpha, beta) modulo L_0
ideas.modern_name: normalization of the GT element f in the commutator subgroup, via the tangential base point 01->

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly ties the indeterminacy mod L_0 in solutions of his loop equations to the choice of a uniformizer at the cusp. This is the conceptual origin of fixing GT elements by a tangential base point, written well before Deligne and Ihara made it standard. The connection is now well known, so this is mainly priority/historical evidence rather than new mathematics.
missed.quote: le choix d'uniformisante de l'anneau local de U^_{0,3} en 0 (disons) détermine un scindage de M_{0,3}^{!an}(0), considéré comme ext. de N_{0,3}^! par L_0 — et il faudra dans la suite essayer de saisir un tel scindage ... comme une façon privilégiée ... de 'normaliser' le choix de (alpha,beta) mod L_0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's early use of tangential base points (around 1981) in the GT setting. It also frames as open how to extend the splitting from Gamma_Q to the whole abstract GT-type group, i.e. a canonical section of GT^[0] over its quotient.

deep.surprise_reason: The ideas (cusp decomposition groups, splitting by a tangential base point, normalization of GT elements) are now standard. Seeing them explicitly linked in Grothendieck's pre-Drinfeld/Deligne notes is a notable historical detail but not new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: The '406' written above 'il' is most likely Grothendieck's own page number (206; the next page is numbered 207), not an inserted word.
'n'y correspondent pas' is crossed out and replaced by 'deux autres', so read: 'il y a deux autres sous-groupes analogues M_{0,3}^{!~}[q], avec q=1, q=inf'.
The superscript in 'M_{0,3}^{!an}(0)' is an insertion of 'an' above '!' ('!an' rather than '!~').
The left-hand side reads '_Q P^1_Q' for U^_{0,3}; the meaning is P^1 over Q.
